description: One recipe from your account: its materials and amounts, colorants, notes, its stated firing (firedAt: the cone scale, the low and optional high cone of the claimed range, the cones actually tested, the atmospheres and processes, and for a temperature the rate and hold; each cone exactly as the potter gave it), whether it is for a food surface, the firing logs it went through with a result note each and, where known, the cone and atmosphere each was fired at, the potter’s summary of how it came out at each cone and atmosphere (coneResults; one outside the stated firing is kept), the firing band and target specific gravity saved with it, and its unity formula worked out afresh. It is checked against the limit set chosen in your settings: for the firing given here, or else the band chosen on the recipe, or else the bands its stated firing falls in (a range across two bands is checked at each). A firing from cone 12 up is band 'top', where no limit set has figures: its limits are not checked, and limitsNote says so. coneFit says, for the same firing, whether the chemistry looks like that firing's, as the recipe page's limits panel does: by Katz's boron rule and Hesselberth & Roy's silica and alumina whatever limit set is chosen, a note (verdict 'cooler' or 'hotter') only when boron and silica or alumina agree on another band, 'closer' when a range across bands looks nearer one end, 'fits' when nothing points away (not a pass), 'skipped' where the published figures do not reach (among them firings cooler than cone 06 or hotter than cone 10). Cone 6 against cone 10 is told apart only roughly (strength 'soft'). A guide, not a test.

firing.description: The firing, as a cone or a temperature. Leave it out when it is not known. From cone 12 up (about 1320 °C) no published glaze limits reach, so the limits are not checked there; the cone check judges cone 06 to 10 only.

chart.description: Which cones the cone is: Orton (the default) or SK (JIS R 8101).

cone.description: An Orton cone from 022 to 42 ("06", "6", "10", "14", a half cone as "5.5"), or with chart "sk" an SK cone (JIS R 8101) from SK 022 to SK 20 ("6a", "8", "14").

language.description: The language for any sentences in the answer, as a BCP 47 tag such as "en", "de" or "ja". Languages Glazecalc does not offer are answered in English.
